commands.name: perl text substitution
commands.description: In-place edits, find and replace, and regex transforms across files using Perl one-liners

patterns.text: replace all tabs with 4 spaces in every python file
patterns.explanation: In-place replaces every tab character with 4 spaces across all .py files

patterns.text: find and replace a string across multiple files recursively
patterns.explanation: Recursively selects ordinary .js files and replaces oldFunction with newFunction in place; matching directory names are skipped.

patterns.text: replace text only on lines matching a condition
patterns.explanation: Replaces localhost with production.host only on lines starting with DB_HOST

patterns.text: do a multiline search and replace across a file
patterns.explanation: Slurps the entire file and replaces everything between BEGIN and END including across lines

patterns.text: convert DOS line endings to Unix line endings
patterns.explanation: Removes carriage returns to convert Windows CRLF to Unix LF line endings

patterns.text: swap two words everywhere in a file
patterns.explanation: Atomically swaps every occurrence of width and height without intermediate collisions

patterns.text: use capture groups to reorder parts of a matched pattern
patterns.explanation: Transforms 'Last, First' into 'First Last' using regex capture groups

patterns.text: strip simple HTML-like tags from text
patterns.explanation: Removes simple angle-bracket tag fragments; it does not parse arbitrary HTML or decode entities.

patterns.text: replace a word with word boundaries in all C source files keeping backups
patterns.explanation: Replaces whole-word foo with bar in all .c files, saving originals as .bak

patterns.text: replace text only on the first line of each file
patterns.command: perl -i -pe 's/PATTERN/REPLACE/ if $. == 1; close ARGV if eof' file1.txt file2.txt
patterns.explanation: Replaces the first match only on the first line of each input file and resets the line counter at each file boundary.

patterns.text: increment every sequence of decimal digits in a file by one
patterns.explanation: Increments each digit sequence independently in place; neighboring signs and decimal points are not parsed as part of a number.

patterns.text: replace text in a binary executable file
patterns.explanation: In-place text replacement inside a binary file, keeping a backup copy

commands.name: perl text extraction
commands.description: Extract specific fields, patterns, emails, IPs, and URLs from text using Perl regex

patterns.text: extract all email addresses from a log file
patterns.explanation: Finds and prints every email address pattern in the file, one per line

patterns.text: extract all IP addresses from a file
patterns.explanation: Extracts dotted-decimal IPv4 addresses with four octets in the range 0–255.

patterns.text: extract all URLs from a document
patterns.explanation: Pulls out all HTTP and HTTPS URLs from the file

patterns.text: extract the second field from each line like awk
patterns.explanation: Auto-splits each line on whitespace and prints the second field (zero-indexed)

patterns.text: extract text between two markers or delimiters
patterns.explanation: Prints all lines from START to END inclusive, using the flip-flop operator

patterns.text: extract the value of a specific key from key=value config lines
patterns.explanation: Captures and prints the value after DB_PASSWORD= from a config file

patterns.text: extract sorted unique ASCII words from a text file
patterns.command: perl -ne '$w{$_}++ for /([a-zA-Z]+)/g; END { print "$_\n" for sort keys %w }' file.txt
patterns.explanation: Collects ASCII-letter words case-sensitively and prints each distinct word in sorted order.

patterns.text: extract specific columns from a colon-delimited file like /etc/passwd
patterns.explanation: Splits each line on colon and prints username (field 0) and UID (field 2)

commands.name: perl line filtering
commands.synopsis: perl -ne 'print if condition' | perl -ne 'print unless condition'
commands.description: Line selection, deduplication, range operations, and line-level filtering with Perl

patterns.text: remove duplicate lines keeping first occurrence and preserving order
patterns.explanation: Tracks seen lines in a hash and only prints each unique line the first time

patterns.text: print specific line range from a file like lines 10 to 20
patterns.explanation: Uses the range operator to print only lines 10 through 20

patterns.text: print every Nth line from a file
patterns.explanation: Prints every 5th line using the line number variable $.

patterns.text: print lines longer than 80 characters
patterns.command: perl -CSD -ne '$line=$_; $line =~ s/\r?\n\z//; print if length($line)>80' file.txt
patterns.explanation: Decodes UTF-8, counts characters after excluding LF/CRLF, and prints original records longer than 80 characters.

patterns.text: print the last 10 lines of a file like tail
patterns.explanation: Reads all lines then prints the last 10 using negative array slicing

patterns.text: remove all blank lines from a file
patterns.explanation: Skips lines that are empty or contain only whitespace

patterns.text: print lines that contain a pattern but not another pattern
patterns.explanation: Shows lines containing error (case insensitive) but excluding those with deprecated

patterns.text: reverse the order of all lines in a file
patterns.explanation: Reads all lines into a list, reverses it, and prints the result

patterns.text: delete content between START and END markers in a file
patterns.explanation: Removes all lines from START to END inclusive using the flip-flop operator

patterns.text: print the first 50 lines of a file then stop
patterns.explanation: Efficiently prints first 50 lines and exits without reading the rest

patterns.text: delete the first 10 lines from a file
patterns.explanation: Removes lines 1 through 10 in-place, keeping a backup

patterns.text: print file content up to a pattern match then stop
patterns.command: perl -ne 'if (/PATTERN/) { close ARGV } else { print }' file.txt
patterns.explanation: Prints all lines until PATTERN is found, then closes the file

patterns.text: find duplicate consecutive words in a text file
patterns.explanation: Finds repeated adjacent words, including across line breaks, and reports the line where each repeated pair starts.

patterns.text: find palindrome words in a dictionary or word list
patterns.explanation: Prints words that read the same forwards and backwards

commands.name: perl text formatting
commands.description: Padding, alignment, case conversion, column manipulation, and output formatting with Perl

patterns.text: convert text to uppercase
patterns.explanation: Converts every line to uppercase using the uc function

patterns.text: convert text to lowercase
patterns.explanation: Converts every line to lowercase using the lc function

patterns.text: capitalize the first letter of every word in a file
patterns.explanation: Title-cases every word by lowercasing then capitalizing the first letter

patterns.text: add line numbers to every line in a file
patterns.explanation: Prepends right-justified 4-digit line numbers to each line

patterns.text: pad each line with trailing spaces to a minimum width of 40 characters
patterns.explanation: Decodes UTF-8 and pads short lines on the right to a minimum of 40 Unicode characters; longer lines are retained and output records end with LF.

patterns.text: format output as aligned columns from whitespace-separated data
patterns.explanation: Formats the first three fields as left-aligned 20 and 10 char columns and a right-aligned 8 char column

patterns.text: trim leading and trailing spaces and tabs without joining lines
patterns.explanation: Removes spaces and tabs at each line edge while preserving LF or CRLF line endings.

patterns.text: squeeze multiple consecutive blank lines into one
patterns.explanation: Uses paragraph mode (-00) to collapse runs of blank lines into a single blank line

patterns.text: add zero-padded line numbers to each line of a file
patterns.explanation: Prepends 4-digit zero-padded line numbers to every line

patterns.text: reverse the order of all lines in a file
patterns.explanation: Reads all lines then prints them in reverse order like tac

patterns.text: reverse characters on each line of a file
patterns.explanation: Reverses the character order within each line

patterns.text: reverse paragraphs in a file
patterns.explanation: Uses paragraph mode (-00) to reverse the order of paragraphs

commands.name: perl csv/data processing
commands.description: CSV parsing, field reordering, data transformation, and tabular data manipulation with Perl

patterns.text: sum the third column of a simple comma-delimited file
patterns.explanation: Splits each line on comma, accumulates the third field, and prints the total; input must not contain CSV quoting, embedded commas, or multiline fields.

patterns.text: reorder three columns in a simple comma-delimited file
patterns.explanation: Prints fields in third, first, second order without moving the original newline into the first field; requires simple unquoted data.

patterns.text: filter simple comma-delimited rows where a column matches a condition
patterns.explanation: Prints only CSV rows where the fourth column value exceeds 100; input must not contain CSV quoting, embedded commas, or multiline fields.

patterns.text: convert simple comma-delimited rows to tab-separated rows
patterns.explanation: Splits simple unquoted rows with trailing empty fields retained, then joins them with tabs.

patterns.text: add a new calculated column to a simple comma-delimited
patterns.explanation: Appends a new column that is the product of the second and third columns; input must not contain CSV quoting, embedded commas, or multiline fields.

patterns.text: extract sorted unique values from the second simple comma-delimited column
patterns.command: perl -F, -lane '$seen{$F[1]}++; END { print for sort keys %seen }' data.csv
patterns.explanation: Collects second-column values without record separators and prints sorted distinct values; requires simple unquoted data.

patterns.text: convert simple UTF-8 comma-delimited data with a header to a JSON array
patterns.command:
perl -CSD -MJSON::PP -ne 's/?
\z//; @f=split /,/, $_, -1; if ($.==1) { @h=@f; for (@h) { die "duplicate header
" if $h{$_}++ } } else { die "column count mismatch
" unless @f==@h; my %row; @row{@h}=@f; push @rows,\%row } END { print JSON::PP->new->canonical->encode(\@rows), "
" }' data.csv
patterns.explanation: Uses the first row as unique object keys and JSON::PP for JSON escaping, removes LF/CRLF before splitting, and accepts simple comma-delimited UTF-8 data without CSV quoting.

patterns.text: group and count simple comma-delimited rows by the first column
patterns.command: perl -F, -lane '$c{$F[0]}++; END { printf "%-20s %d\n", $_, $c{$_} for sort keys %c }' data.csv
patterns.explanation: Counts first-field values after removing record separators; requires simple unquoted data.

patterns.text: print specific columns from a tab-separated file like columns 1 2 and last
patterns.explanation: Splits on tabs and prints the first, second, and last fields

patterns.text: print a range of columns from a tab-delimited file
patterns.explanation: Outputs the first 20 columns from tab-separated data

patterns.text: delete all columns after column N in a tab-separated file
patterns.command: perl -i -ne 's/\r?\n\z//; @f=split /\t/, $_, -1; splice @f,5 if @f>5; print join("\t", @f), "\n"' data.tsv
patterns.explanation: Edits data.tsv in place, retaining up to its first five fields without padding short rows; preserves trailing empty retained fields and writes one LF per row.

patterns.text: insert a new column after a specific position in a TSV file
patterns.command: perl -i -ne 's/\r?\n\z//; @f=split /\t/, $_, -1; push @f,"" while @f<3; splice @f,3,0,"new_value"; print join("\t", @f), "\n"' data.tsv
patterns.explanation: Edits data.tsv in place, inserts new_value as the fourth field, keeps trailing empty fields, and writes one LF per row; rows shorter than three fields are padded with empty fields.

commands.name: perl file operations
commands.description: Batch rename files, file stats, recursive file manipulation, and filesystem operations with Perl

patterns.text: batch rename files replacing spaces with underscores
patterns.explanation: Iterates over all files in the current directory and renames those with spaces

patterns.text: rename files changing extension from .txt to .md
patterns.explanation: Renames all .txt files to .md by substituting the extension

patterns.text: add the backup_ prefix to JPEG filenames in the current directory
patterns.explanation: Prepends 'backup_' to matching .jpg filenames in the current directory; it does not add a suffix.

patterns.text: lowercase all filenames in the current directory
patterns.explanation: Renames every file to its lowercase equivalent

patterns.text: recursively find ordinary files larger than 10 MiB
patterns.explanation: Walks the current tree and prints ordinary files larger than 10*1024*1024 bytes.

patterns.text: recursively replace a string in all files of a specific type
patterns.command: perl -MFile::Find -e 'find({no_chdir=>1,wanted=>sub { return unless -f $_ && !-l $_ && /\.html\z/; local @ARGV=($_); local $^I=".bak"; local $_; while (<>) { s/old/new/g; print } }}, ".")'
patterns.explanation: Walks nested paths without changing directories, edits only ordinary non-symlink .html files, and keeps .bak backups; directories with an .html suffix are skipped.

patterns.text: number files sequentially like photo001.jpg photo002.jpg
patterns.explanation: Renames all jpg files to sequentially numbered filenames with zero-padded numbers

patterns.text: find files containing a pattern in their first N lines
patterns.command: perl -ne 'if (/PATTERN/) { print "$ARGV\n"; close ARGV } elsif ($. >= 10 || eof) { close ARGV }' *.txt
patterns.explanation: Prints each filename at most once when PATTERN occurs within its first ten lines; resets the counter after every file, including short files.

patterns.text: insert a line of text at a specific line number in a file
patterns.command: perl -i -pe 'print "new line here\n" if $. == 5; $. = 0 if eof' file.txt
patterns.explanation: Inserts text before line 5, resetting line counter between files

patterns.text: list ordinary log files smaller than 1000 bytes in the current directory
patterns.explanation: Checks file types and sizes directly, preserving filenames containing spaces; only non-hidden *.log entries are selected.

commands.name: perl math and counting
commands.description: Sums, averages, frequency counts, statistics, and histogram generation using Perl one-liners

patterns.text: sum all numbers in a file one per line
patterns.explanation: Accumulates each line as a number and prints the total sum

patterns.text: calculate the average of a column of numbers
patterns.explanation: Sums all values and divides by count to compute the mean

patterns.text: find the minimum and maximum values in a column
patterns.command: perl -ne 'chomp; $min=$_ if !defined $min || $_<$min; $max=$_ if !defined $max || $_>$max; END { print "min=$min max=$max\n" }' numbers.txt
patterns.explanation: Tracks the running minimum and maximum and prints both at the end

patterns.text: count word frequency in a text file
patterns.command: perl -ne '$freq{lc $_}++ for /([\w]+)/g; END { printf "%6d %s\n", $freq{$_}, $_ for sort { $freq{$b}<=>$freq{$a} } keys %freq }' file.txt
patterns.explanation: Counts each word case-insensitively and prints frequencies sorted most to least common

patterns.text: generate a text histogram of value frequencies
patterns.command: perl -ne 'chomp; $h{$_}++; END { printf "%-20s %s\n", $_, "#" x $h{$_} for sort keys %h }' data.txt
patterns.explanation: Counts occurrences of each unique line and draws a horizontal bar chart with # symbols

patterns.text: calculate the median of a list of numbers
patterns.command: perl -e '@n=sort {$a<=>$b} map { chomp; $_ } <>; die "no numbers\n" unless @n; $m=int(@n/2); print((@n%2 ? $n[$m] : ($n[$m-1]+$n[$m])/2), "\n")' numbers.txt
patterns.explanation: Sorts numeric input, selects the central value for odd counts, averages the two central values for even counts, and rejects empty input.

patterns.text: count the number of lines in a file
patterns.explanation: Uses the special $. variable which holds the current line number to report total lines

patterns.text: sum the size column of the current non-recursive ls listing in MiB
patterns.explanation: Sums the size column from ls -l, without recursive traversal or hidden names, and divides by 1048576.

patterns.text: sum a range of columns and append the total
patterns.explanation: Sums columns 3 through 6 and appends the total as a new column

patterns.text: find the median value from a list of numbers
patterns.command: sort -n data.txt | perl -e '@n=<>; chomp @n; die "no numbers\n" unless @n; $m=int(@n/2); print((@n%2 ? $n[$m] : ($n[$m-1]+$n[$m])/2), "\n")'
patterns.explanation: Numerically sorts input, then computes a true odd/even median instead of selecting only the lower central value.

patterns.text: calculate percentage distribution of values
patterns.command: sort data.txt | uniq -c | perl -ne '($n,$v)=/^\s*(\d+)\s+(.*)/; $s+=$n; push @r,[$n,$v]; END{printf "%s: %.1f%%\n",$$_[1],100*$$_[0]/$s for @r}'
patterns.explanation: Counts occurrences and shows each value with its percentage of the total

patterns.text: group numbers into thousand-wide buckets by truncation toward zero
patterns.explanation: Truncates each number divided by 1000 toward zero, multiplies back by 1000, then counts bucket frequencies.

patterns.text: count case-insensitive whitespace-delimited token frequencies
patterns.command: perl -lane '$c{lc$_}++ for @F; END{printf "%4d %s\n",$c{$_},$_ for sort{$c{$b}<=>$c{$a}}keys%c}' file.txt
patterns.explanation: Splits each line on whitespace, folds token case, retains punctuation inside tokens, and sorts by descending frequency.

patterns.text: print the minimum and maximum values from a list of numbers
patterns.explanation: Tracks running min and max across all input lines

patterns.text: calculate the average of numbers from stdin
patterns.explanation: Accumulates sum and count, prints the mean at the end

commands.name: perl string manipulation
commands.description: Reverse strings, encode/decode data, transliteration, and character-level operations with Perl

patterns.text: reverse each line of text in a file
patterns.explanation: Reverses the character order of each line

patterns.text: base64 encode a string or file
patterns.explanation: Reads the entire file and prints its base64 encoded representation

patterns.text: base64 decode a string
patterns.explanation: Decodes a base64 encoded string back to its original form

patterns.text: URL encode a string for use in a web request
patterns.explanation: Percent-encodes special characters for safe use in URLs

patterns.text: URL decode a percent-encoded string
patterns.explanation: Converts percent-encoded characters back to their original form

patterns.text: ROT13 encode or decode text
patterns.explanation: Applies ROT13 cipher using transliteration, works for both encoding and decoding

patterns.text: generate a random password of a given length
patterns.explanation: Generates a 20-character random password from upper, lower, digits, and symbols

patterns.text: convert hex string to ASCII text
patterns.explanation: Packs a hexadecimal string into its ASCII byte representation

patterns.text: ROT13 encode a file in place
patterns.explanation: Applies ROT13 cipher to all letters in the file

patterns.text: convert a string to its ASCII ordinal values
patterns.explanation: Splits string into chars and prints the ASCII value of each

patterns.text: convert ASCII ordinal values back to a string
patterns.explanation: Converts a list of numbers to their character equivalents

commands.name: perl log analysis
commands.synopsis: perl -ne 'log parsing expression' | perl -ane 'log field extraction'
commands.description: Parse log files, extract timestamps, count errors, and analyze patterns in log data with Perl

patterns.text: count occurrences of each HTTP status code in an access log
patterns.command: perl -ane '$c{$F[8]}++; END { printf "%s: %d\n", $_, $c{$_} for sort keys %c }' access.log
patterns.explanation: Extracts the HTTP status code field and counts each unique code

patterns.text: find the top 10 most frequent IP addresses in a web server log
patterns.command: perl -ane '$ip{$F[0]}++; END { @ips=sort {$ip{$b}<=>$ip{$a} || $a cmp $b} keys %ip; for ($i=0; $i<@ips && $i<10; $i++) { printf "%-16s %d\n", $ips[$i], $ip{$ips[$i]} } }' access.log
patterns.explanation: Prints up to ten real IP keys ordered by request count, breaking ties by address; short and empty logs do not create missing entries.

patterns.text: extract all error messages from a log file with timestamps
patterns.explanation: Prints log lines containing ERROR, FATAL, or CRITICAL severity levels

patterns.text: show requests per hour from an Apache or Nginx access log
patterns.command: perl -ne '$h{$1}++ if m{(\d{2}/\w+/\d{4}:\d{2})}; END { printf "%s: %d\n", $_, $h{$_} for sort keys %h }' access.log
patterns.explanation: Extracts the date:hour portion of timestamps and counts requests per hour

patterns.text: find all unique user agents in an access log
patterns.explanation: Extracts the user agent string from the last quoted field of each log line

patterns.text: calculate average response time from log entries
patterns.command: perl -ne 'while (/(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)ms/g) { $t+=$1; $n++ } END { die "no timing samples\n" unless $n; printf "avg: %.1fms\n", $t/$n }' app.log
patterns.explanation: Averages all nonnegative integer or decimal millisecond values found in the log and rejects input with no timing samples.

patterns.text: show log entries from the last hour only
patterns.explanation: Interprets leading timestamps in local time and selects only records from now back to less than one hour ago, excluding future records.

patterns.text: group and count log messages by error type ignoring details
patterns.command: perl -ne 'if (/(?:ERROR|WARN).*?:\s*(.+?)(?:\s*at\s|$)/) { $c{$1}++ } END { printf "%5d %s\n", $c{$_}, $_ for sort { $c{$b}<=>$c{$a} } keys %c }' app.log
patterns.explanation: Normalizes error messages by stripping stack trace details and counts each unique type

commands.name: perl network/sysadmin
commands.description: IP extraction, URL parsing, config file editing, and system administration tasks with Perl

patterns.text: extract and sort all unique IP addresses from a file
patterns.explanation: Extracts distinct dotted-decimal IPv4 addresses with octets 0–255, then sorts by their four numeric components.

patterns.text: convert a subnet CIDR notation to IP range
patterns.explanation: Calculates the first and last IP address in a CIDR subnet range

patterns.text: check which ports are open on localhost
patterns.explanation: Scans TCP ports 1-1024 on localhost and reports which ones accept connections

patterns.text: set max_connections to 200 only in the mysqld section of a MySQL config
patterns.explanation: Tracks INI section headers and edits max_connections only within [mysqld], leaving similarly named settings in other sections unchanged.

patterns.text: show all listening network connections with their PIDs
patterns.explanation: Formats netstat output into a clean table of protocol, address, and PID

patterns.text: check a simplified email address pattern
patterns.explanation: Tests a simplified email-like syntax; it is not complete standards validation or a mailbox existence check.

patterns.text: extract domain names from a list of URLs
patterns.explanation: Extracts host fragments from every simple HTTP/HTTPS URL on each line, without path or port.

patterns.text: comment out a specific line in a config file
patterns.explanation: Comments matching PermitRootLogin lines, including indented settings; this removes the explicit setting rather than guaranteeing a particular default policy.

commands.name: perl json/xml processing
commands.description: JSON manipulation, XML extraction, and structured data processing with Perl one-liners

patterns.text: pretty print a JSON file
patterns.explanation: Reads JSON from stdin, parses it, and outputs with indentation and formatting

patterns.text: extract a specific field from a JSON file
patterns.explanation: Parses JSON and prints the value of the name field

patterns.text: convert a JSON array of flat objects to quoted CSV rows
patterns.command: perl -MJSON::PP -e 'local $/; $d=decode_json(<STDIN>); binmode STDOUT, ":encoding(UTF-8)"; @keys=sort keys %{$d->[0] // {}}; for $row (@$d) { @v=map { defined $row->{$_} ? $row->{$_} : "" } @keys; for (@v) { s/"/""/g; $_=qq("$_") } print join(",", @v), "\n" }' < data.json
patterns.explanation: Uses sorted keys from the first object, emits no header, doubles embedded quotes, and quotes values containing line breaks; input fields must be scalar.

patterns.text: merge two JSON files together
patterns.command:
perl -MJSON::PP -e 'local $/; @ARGV==2 or die "usage: a.json b.json
"; open my $a,"<",$ARGV[0] or die $!; open my $b,"<",$ARGV[1] or die $!; $x=decode_json(<$a>); $y=decode_json(<$b>); ref($x) eq "HASH" && ref($y) eq "HASH" or die "JSON objects required
"; print encode_json({%$x,%$y}), "
"' a.json b.json
patterns.explanation: Reads two JSON objects independently and merges top-level keys, with keys from the second file taking precedence.

patterns.text: filter a JSON array keeping only matching objects
patterns.explanation: Filters a JSON array to include only objects where status equals active

patterns.text: extract all values for a specific key from nested JSON
patterns.command: perl -MJSON::PP -e 'local $/; $d=decode_json(<STDIN>); sub f{my$d=shift;if(ref$d eq"HASH"){print "$d->{$ARGV[0]}\n" if exists$d->{$ARGV[0]};f($_)for values%$d}elsif(ref$d eq"ARRAY"){f($_)for@$d}} f($d)' name < data.json
patterns.explanation: Recursively walks a JSON structure and prints every occurrence of the specified key

patterns.text: count objects in a JSON array grouped by a field value
patterns.command: perl -MJSON::PP -e 'local $/; $d=decode_json(<STDIN>); $c{$_->{type}}++ for @$d; printf "%-20s %d\n",$_,$c{$_} for sort keys %c' < data.json
patterns.explanation: Groups JSON array objects by their type field and prints counts for each value

patterns.text: extract text between simple title tags in an XML-like file
patterns.explanation: Extracts multiline content between exact <title> and </title> tags; attributes, namespaces and XML entity decoding require a real XML parser.

commands.name: perl date/time
commands.description: Date formatting, epoch conversion, duration calculation, and time manipulation with Perl

patterns.text: convert unix epoch timestamp to human readable date
patterns.explanation: Converts a Unix epoch timestamp to a human-readable local time string

patterns.text: get the current date and time in ISO 8601 format
patterns.explanation: Prints the current date and time formatted as ISO 8601 with timezone offset

patterns.text: convert a human readable date to unix epoch timestamp
patterns.explanation: Parses a date string and outputs the corresponding Unix epoch seconds

patterns.text: calculate the number of days between two dates
patterns.explanation: Parses two dates and computes the difference in days

patterns.text: add or subtract days from a date
patterns.command: perl -e 'use Time::Piece; use Time::Seconds; $t=Time::Piece->strptime($ARGV[0],"%Y-%m-%d") + ONE_DAY*$ARGV[1]; print $t->strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), "\n"' '2024-06-15' 30
patterns.explanation: Adds the specified number of days to a date and prints the result

patterns.text: format seconds into human readable hours minutes seconds duration
patterns.explanation: Converts total seconds into a human-readable days/hours/minutes/seconds format

patterns.text: show the day of the week for a given date
patterns.explanation: Parses a date string and prints the full day name like Monday or Friday

patterns.text: convert timestamps in a log file from epoch to readable dates
patterns.explanation: Converts standalone ten-digit sequences to local dates, without matching inside longer digit sequences.

commands.name: perl spacing
commands.description: Add or remove vertical spacing in text files using Perl one-liners

patterns.text: double-space a file
patterns.explanation: Appends an extra newline after each line

patterns.text: double-space a file except blank lines
patterns.explanation: Only adds spacing after lines containing non-whitespace

patterns.text: triple-space a file
patterns.explanation: Appends two extra newlines after each line

patterns.text: remove all blank lines from a file
patterns.explanation: Only prints lines that contain non-whitespace characters

patterns.text: remove all consecutive blank lines leaving just one
patterns.explanation: Paragraph mode collapses multiple blank lines into a single separator

patterns.text: compress multiple blank lines into a single blank line
patterns.explanation: Shortest form using paragraph slurp mode to normalize spacing

patterns.text: calculate the least common multiple of two numbers
patterns.command: perl -le 'sub g { my ($a,$b)=map {abs} @_; ($a,$b)=($b,$a%$b) while $b; return $a } @ARGV==2 or die "two integers required\n"; for (@ARGV) { /\A-?\d+\z/ or die "integers required\n" } ($a,$b)=@ARGV; print(($a==0 || $b==0) ? 0 : abs($a/g($a,$b)*$b))' -- 36 24
patterns.explanation: Computes abs(a/GCD(a,b)*b) for two integers, returning zero when either input is zero.

patterns.text: generate all permutations of a list
patterns.command: perl -e 'sub p { return ([]) unless @_; my @out; for my $i (0..$#_) { my @rest=@_; my $item=splice(@rest,$i,1); push @out, map {[$item,@$_]} p(@rest) } return @out } print join(" ", @$_), "\n" for p(@ARGV)' 1 2 3 4
patterns.explanation: Recursively removes and remembers each chosen element, then prepends it to all permutations of the remaining input.

patterns.text: calculate the power set of a set
patterns.command: perl -le '@a=@ARGV; for $i (0..2**@a-1) { print join ",", map {$a[$_]} grep {$i & (1<<$_)} 0..$#a }' a b c d
patterns.explanation: Uses bitmasks to enumerate subsets of the actual command-line elements, including the empty subset.
